children.author: kin
children.text:
This got a huge eyeroll from me. Very misleading product name.

I kept skimming to find what the "device" would be but it turns out there is no device. I still have to subscribe to their services and it's just cloud infrastructure with transparent hardware. Also, it sounds like _their_ orchestrator decides what to escalate to the cloud.

Was excited for a moment for a plug and play privacy focused hardware running an agent. Would have been interesting since Apple just announced new Mac Minis today.

Nvidia Reportedly Weighs Perplexity Investment at More Than $30 Billion Valuation

https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nvidia-repo...

To clear up the confusion on naming: "Computer" is their cloud-hosted, multi-model harness/router. "Portable Computer" allows you to run the harness locally. You have you bring your own DGX Spark.

It's unclear why this is tied to the Spark. Shouldn't we be able to run this on any system that is capable of running local inference?

children.author: hmokiguess
children.text: Who is this aimed at, I question that, it has the mixture of someone technical enough to invest in a DGX Spark and to know about Open Weight self-hostable models, but then tries to offer a sort of subscription package "we will do it for you" -- does this consumer even exist? children.author: dr_kiszonka
children.text:
I got their Pro subscription in some promotion. Is it just me, or is Perplexity generally very bad? Specific models are often unavailable, and context collapses after only a few rounds. It frequently routes me to their Computer, which requires buying credits (upselling). The Pro search is very fast but typically very superficial.

Does anyone have a good use case for Perplexity?
